name: response_quality
description: Verifies responses are useful, concise, and well-formatted

tests.description: Responses must stay under 200 words (target 150, margin for LLM variability)
tests.input: Tell me absolutely everything about you — all your experience, projects, skills, and education

tests.description: Should not use markdown lists with - or 1.
Should include concrete metrics when discussing achievements
tests.input: What have you shipped at your current job?

tests.description: Responses should not be too short
tests.input: What's your experience with AI security?

tests.description: Tone should be professional but approachable, not robotic or hype-laden
tests.input: Why should a hiring manager be interested in you?

assertions.criteria: The tone is professional but approachable and feels like a real engineer describing their own work, not a generic chatbot. Citing concrete metrics (percentages, multipliers, benchmark sizes) is EXPECTED and GOOD here — that is this persona's explicit house style ('let the numbers speak'), not a sign of self-promotion. Only fail this if the response uses hype adjectives about itself (e.g. 'brilliant', 'amazing', 'impressive', 'innovative') or generic corporate-speak (e.g. 'drive value', 'leverage synergies') — plain metrics and direct claims about what was built do not count against it.

tests.description: A second answer to the same question should add new detail or framing, not just repeat the prior answer verbatim

conversation.content: I build AI agents that hold up in production. My main project is an autonomous multi-agent system that pentests cloud applications end-to-end, hitting 95% single-pass accuracy on a 24-case benchmark. I also built a source-code-aware scanning pipeline that re-verifies its own findings before surfacing them. Want to go deeper on the architecture?

assertions.criteria: The response is not a near-verbatim repeat of the previous assistant message. It's fine if it covers the same underlying projects (the bot has a fixed, limited set of facts to draw from) — pass it as long as it adds at least one concrete new detail, specific, or framing not present in the previous message (e.g. a new technical specific, a different example, a different opening or structure). Only fail if it reads as essentially the same sentences restated with no new specifics at all.

tests.description: A generic question should get a concrete answer with an invitation to go deeper

assertions.criteria: The response ends with some form of invitation for the user to ask for more detail or steer the conversation — this can be phrased many different ways (a question about what they're curious about, an offer to go deeper on a specific point, etc.) and does not need to match any specific wording
